R004.justification: A finite rational spanning set yields a basis by successively removing dependent vectors. Gaussian elimination shows an independent family in ℚ^t has size at most t, proving strong rank for ℚ and invariance of finite basis size. If an injective matrix R^s→R^t had a nonzero rational kernel vector, multiplying it by a common nonzero integer denominator would give a nonzero kernel vector in R^s. Its rational extension is thus injective, so s≤t. This proves strong rank for R; comparison of finite bases consequently identifies the rank and its natural conversion with n. Isomorphisms carry bases to bases.

R004.fact: In a one-dimensional ℚ-subspace of ℂ, every nonzero a spans the space, so each nonzero g has the form g=qa for a nonzero rational q. A nonzero finitely generated module has a finite nonempty generating tuple with all entries nonzero.

grounds.reason: J is nonzero and finitely generated.
Multiplication embeds QJ as the rational span of J.
That space has dimension one.

R004.justification: The single nonzero vector a is independent over ℚ and hence is a basis in dimension one; the coordinate of a nonzero g cannot be zero. Removing zero elements from a finite generating family preserves its span, and an empty remaining family would generate only the zero module, contrary to nonzeroness.

R004.fact: If p is prime and q∈ℚ is nonzero, then q=p^ηu for some η∈ℤ and u with both numerator and denominator prime to p; consequently u,u⁻¹∈ℤ_(p).

grounds.reason: p is prime, in particular p≥2.
Membership in R is specified by a denominator not divisible by p.
Each q_j is a nonzero rational.

R004.justification: Write q=m/d with nonzero integers m,d. Repeated division by p terminates because absolute values strictly decrease when divisible, giving m=p^αm₀ and d=p^βd₀ with α,β≥0 and p dividing neither m₀ nor d₀. Set η=α−β and u=m₀/d₀. The two denominators d₀,m₀ show that u and u⁻¹ lie in R. These powers are in ℚ⊂ℂ, so even negative exponents are defined and nonzero. The finite minimum argument and the two module inclusions are already proved in S004.

R005.fact: For modules over commutative rings, a balanced additive pure-tensor formula induces a unique additive map on the tensor product, and equality on pure tensors implies equality of maps. In the present maps, compatibility with the K factor makes the induced maps K-linear. Applying an additive lattice operator to the M factor commutes with these scalar maps; an R-linear operator on M_R also descends to M_R/pM_R and commutes with the quotient tensor maps.

V_K is M tensor_Z K.
All specified lattice operators preserve M and M_R; E_ij preserves M_R.
The maps and kappa compatibility are given explicitly.
The quotient maps are given explicitly and multiples of p tensor to zero.

R005.justification: The tensor product is generated by pure tensors modulo additivity and balancing relations. The displayed formulas respect those relations, so descend uniquely; composites fixing the generators are identity maps. Acting on the module factor commutes with changing scalar factors. For an R-linear A, A(pu)=pA(u), giving a quotient operator and the same compatibility on quotient generators.

R005.fact: If (a_i) over the finite index set I is an R-basis of an R-module L and kappa:R->K is a unital ring map, then (a_i tensor 1) is a K-basis of L tensor_R K. Every R-linear identity between operators on L remains an identity after scalar extension, with R coefficients mapped by kappa.

F001 identifies M_R tensor_R K with V_K compatibly with lattice operators.

R005.justification: Write u=sum_i c_i a_i; then u tensor d=sum_i a_i tensor kappa(c_i)d, proving spanning. Each coordinate functional L->R induces L tensor_R K->K and evaluates a_j tensor 1 to delta_ij, proving independence. R005.fact: In a field K of prime characteristic p, an integer a has zero image exactly when p divides a. Hence if 0<=r<p, the integer r! has nonzero image in K, including 0!=1. A unital ring map R->K sends each unit of R to a unit of K, and therefore to a nonzero element.

0<=lambda<p, and the local index r lies between 0 and lambda.
Each binom(lambda,j) used is a unit in R.

R005.justification: Divide an integer by p; its image is the image of its remainder. By the defining minimal positive characteristic, no remainder from 1 through p-1 is zero, so the kernel is pZ. Every factor 1,...,r is consequently nonzero; a finite product of nonzero field elements is nonzero. For a unit t with inverse s, kappa(t)kappa(s)=1, so kappa(t) is invertible and cannot be zero in a field.

R006.fact: A K-linear map A satisfies A(Σ_k c_k beta_k)=Σ_k c_k A(beta_k) for a finite family. A K-linear subspace containing every element of a basis equals the whole ambient vector space.

R006.fact: A vector space of positive finite dimension is nonzero. For a K-linear action of a Lie algebra spanned over K by x,y,h, a K-linear subspace is invariant under the entire Lie algebra if and only if it is invariant under x,y,h.

Each tensor of a lattice element ax+by+ch expands into a K-linear combination of the three tensor generators, and sums of such tensors span L_K. argument.text: H002 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We establish the lowering-power identities by simultaneous induction on t≥0. At t=0, H004 gives hv=λv and xv=0. In the induction step assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v when t≥1, with xv=0 when t=0. The commutators of H003 give h y^(t+1)v=(yh−2y)y^t v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. Also x y^(t+1)v=(yx+h)y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. For t=0 the yxv term is zero directly, and the same coefficient formula holds. Discharge L1 and apply induction: both identities hold for every t in their stated ranges.

argument.text: Set QJ=ℚ⊗_R J. By N003, the images 1⊗c0 of a finite generating set of J span QJ over ℚ, so QJ is finite-dimensional. The multiplication map is given on pure tensors by ρ⊗c0↦ρc0∈ℂ, with ρ∈ℚ and c0∈J; it is well-defined by R-balancing. 1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 300 seconds, and use Lean's finite default heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.
46: 
47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and independent endpoint-fidelity Audit B remain required.

Also x y^(t+1)v=(yx+h)y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. For t=0 the yxv term is zero directly, and the same coefficient formula holds. Each factor is a nonzero complex integer, and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L2 proves linear independence. There are n vectors by F001 and dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n by H003; a linearly independent family of this size is a basis. Thus (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V.

Set z=y^(λ+1)v. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Expand z in the basis F003. For every coordinate i∈I, its coefficient is annihilated by (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i), a nonzero complex integer. Division by i! in F001 now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

Iterating the formulas in F004 and dividing by r! gives, for every natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i, and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) when i+r≤λ. The coefficients are the successive products (λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r! and (i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!, respectively, hence the displayed integer binomial coefficients; when r=0 both products are one. If r>i then the x string reaches xe_0=0; if i+r>λ then the y string reaches ye_λ=0. Thus both out-of-range expressions are zero. Together with F001–F004 these are all the asserted coordinate and basis formulas.

Since ℚ is the fraction field of R⊂ℚ (H001), a common nonzero denominator in R combines any finite tensor sum into d0^(-1)⊗c0 with 0≠d0∈R and c0∈J. Let r=dim_ℚ QJ. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=ℚ, C=M_R. The rings R and ℚ are nontrivial commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: an injective finite matrix over R remains injective over ℚ by clearing denominators of a hypothetical kernel vector, and the dimension inequality over ℚ then gives the required rank inequality; the inclusion R→ℚ gives the algebra structure. 23: instance (p : ℕ) : Subsingleton (Algebra (ZMod p) R) :=
24:   ⟨fun _ _ => Algebra.algebra_ext _ _ <| RingHom.congr_fun <| Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩

28: variable {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ) [CharP R m]
29: 
30: /-- The `ZMod n`-algebra structure on rings whose characteristic `m` divides `n`.
31: See note [reducible non-instances]. -/
32: abbrev algebra' (h : m ∣ n) : Algebra (ZMod n) R where
33:   algebraMap := ZMod.castHom h R
34:   smul := fun a r => cast a * r
35:   commutes' := fun a r =>
36:     show (cast a * r : R) = r * cast a by
37:       rcases ZMod.intCast_surjective a with ⟨k, rfl⟩
38:       change ZMod.castHom h R k * r = r * ZMod.castHom h R k
39:       rw [map_intCast, Int.cast_comm]
40:   smul_def' := fun _ _ => rfl
41: 
42: end
43: 
44: /-- The `ZMod p`-algebra structure on a ring of characteristic `p`. This is not an
45: instance since it creates a diamond with `Algebra.id`.
46: See note [reducible non-instances]. -/
47: abbrev algebra (p : ℕ) [CharP R p] : Algebra (ZMod p) R :=
48:   algebra' R p dvd_rfl
49: 
50: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
51: /-- Any ring with a `ZMod p`-module structure can be upgraded to a `ZMod p`-algebra. Not an
52: instance because this is usually not the default way, and this will cause typeclass search loop. -/
53: @[implicit_reducible]
54: def algebraOfModule (n : ℕ) (R : Type*) [Ring R] [Module (ZMod n) R] : Algebra (ZMod n) R :=
55:   Algebra.ofModule' (proof · · |>.1) (proof · · |>.2) where
56:   proof (r : ZMod n) (x : R) : r • 1 * x = r • x ∧ x * r • 1 = r • x := by
57:     obtain _ | n := n
58:     · obtain rfl : ((inferInstance : Module ℤ R)) = ‹_› := Subsingleton.elim _ _
59:       simp [ZMod, Int.cast_comm]
60:     · obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := ZMod.natCast_zmod_surjective r
61:       simp [Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul, Nat.cast_comm]
62: 
63: instance instIsScalarTower (n : ℕ) (R M : Type*) [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M]
64:     [Module (ZMod n) R] [m₁ : Module (ZMod n) M] [Module R M] :
65:     IsScalarTower (ZMod n) R M := by
66:   let := ZMod.algebraOfModule n R
67:   let m₂ := Module.compHom M (algebraMap (ZMod n) R)
68:   obtain rfl : m₁ = m₂ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
69:   exact ⟨fun x y z ↦ by rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_smul]; rfl⟩
70: 
71: end ZMod

185: /-- `b.reindex (e : ι ≃ ι')` is a basis indexed by `ι'` -/
186: def reindex : Basis ι' R M :=
187:   .ofRepr (b.repr.trans (Finsupp.domLCongr e))
188: 
189: theorem reindex_apply (i' : ι') : b.reindex e i' = b (e.symm i') :=
190:   show (b.repr.trans (Finsupp.domLCongr e)).symm (Finsupp.single i' 1) =
191:     b.repr.symm (Finsupp.single (e.symm i') 1)
192:   by rw [LinearEquiv.symm_trans_apply, Finsupp.domLCongr_symm, Finsupp.domLCongr_single]
193: 
194: @[simp]
195: theorem coe_reindex : (b.reindex e : ι' → M) = b ∘ e.symm :=
196:   funext (b.reindex_apply e)
197: 
198: theorem repr_reindex_apply (i' : ι') : (b.reindex e).repr x i' = b.repr x (e.symm i') :=
199:   show (Finsupp.domLCongr e : _ ≃ₗ[R] _) (b.repr x) i' = _ by simp
200: 
201: @[simp]
202: theorem repr_reindex : (b.reindex e).repr x = (b.repr x).mapDomain e :=
203:   DFunLike.ext _ _ <| by simp [repr_reindex_apply]
204: 
205: @[simp]
206: theorem reindex_refl : b.reindex (Equiv.refl ι) = b := by
207:   simp [reindex]
208: 
209: /-- `simp` can prove this as `Basis.coe_reindex` + `EquivLike.range_comp` -/
210: theorem range_reindex : Set.range (b.reindex e) = Set.range b := by
211:   simp [coe_reindex, range_comp]
212: 
213: end Reindex
214: 
215: end Basis

223: /-- A module over `R` with a finite basis is linearly equivalent to functions from its basis to `R`.
224: -/
225: def Basis.equivFun [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R M) : M ≃ₗ[R] ι → R :=
226:   LinearEquiv.trans b.repr
227:     ({ Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite with
228:         toFun := (↑)
229:         map_add' := Finsupp.coe_add
230:         map_smul' := Finsupp.coe_smul } :
231:       (ι →₀ R) ≃ₗ[R] ι → R)
232: 
233: /-- A module over a finite ring that admits a finite basis is finite. -/
234: @[implicit_reducible]
235: def fintypeOfFintype [Fintype ι] (b : Basis ι R M) [Fintype R] : Fintype M :=
236:   haveI := Classical.decEq ι
237:   Fintype.ofEquiv _ b.equivFun.toEquiv.symm
238: 
239: /-- Given a basis `v` indexed by `ι`, the canonical linear equivalence between `ι → R` and `M` maps
240: a function `x : ι → R` to the linear combination `∑_i x i • v i`. -/
241: @[simp]
242: theorem Basis.equivFun_symm_apply [Fintype ι] (b : Basis ι R M) (x : ι → R) :
243:     b.equivFun.symm x = ∑ i, x i • b i := by
244:   simp [Basis.equivFun, Finsupp.linearCombination_apply, sum_fintype, equivFunOnFinite]

representations_and_conversion_obligatio.notes: The endpoint correspondence is mathematically faithful in both directions. Submodule ℤ V describes arbitrary additive subgroups. Fin(l.toNat+1) is the complete integer interval under H002; T001 explicitly supplies both directions of that identification. The generator formulas include both endpoints and all out-of-range divided-power cases. R is a concrete rational subring, with its fraction description assigned to T006; excluded divisibility also excludes zero denominators. MR is the actual tensor R⊗ℤ M, and T006 proves the specified iota injective with image L before the image model is used. J is exactly the preimage of L under c↦c eᵢ. T012 gives the actual rational tensor multiplication, injectivity and image; T013–T016 derive rank one and a principal coefficient module rather than assume them. T017 specifies canonical tensor maps and intertwining for every integral endomorphism; T018's surjection and kernel identify Red with MR/pMR. T019–T020 retain actual lattice basis provenance through iota and scalar extension. VK=K⊗ℤ M agrees with the source through the tensor commutor. LiftOf forces the unique restriction to M, and the conclusion includes existence, so its universal quantification over compatible lifts is not vacuous. Nontrivial and SimpleTriple express exactly the source's nonzero space and all-subspace dichotomy. Pinned Mathlib definitions confirm right-factor-first endomorphism multiplication, scalar-first baseChange, genuine basis coordinates, and the characteristic-p ZMod algebra action. All conversions are planned proof obligations, not extra hypotheses; their bodies are not certified by this review.
